name: United Kingdom — British parties
intro: compare it with British political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of United Kingdom: those represented in the House of Commons and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the House of Commons after the July 2024 general election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 650 members. The Commons sits on facing benches; seats are shown as a hemicycle for comparison.

Green.name: Green Party of England and Wales
Green.priorities: Climate action, Taxing wealth, Public services, Affordable housing, Closer ties with the EU
Green.description: The green party of England and Wales. It calls for wealth taxes, public ownership of water and rail, rapid decarbonisation and rejoining the EU in the long run.

SNP.name: Scottish National Party
SNP.priorities: Scottish independence, Public services, Closer ties with the EU, Climate action
SNP.description: The party of Scottish independence, in government in Scotland since 2007. Centre-left and strongly pro-European, it wants an independent Scotland to rejoin the EU.

Plaid.name: Plaid Cymru
Plaid.ideologies: Welsh nationalism, Social democracy, Green politics, Pro-Europeanism
Plaid.priorities: More powers for Wales, Public services, Climate action, Closer ties with the EU
Plaid.description: Welsh nationalist party that seeks more powers and, eventually, independence for Wales. Centre-left, pro-European and committed to the Welsh language.

Lab.name: Labour Party
Lab.priorities: Public healthcare, Cost of living, Affordable housing, Workers' rights and wages, Fiscal discipline
Lab.description: The main party of the British centre-left, in government since its 2024 landslide. Under Keir Starmer it pairs strict fiscal rules with investment in the NHS, clean energy and housing, and a closer but non-member relationship with the EU.

LD.name: Liberal Democrats
LD.priorities: Public healthcare, Climate action, Civil liberties, Closer ties with the EU, Democratic reform
LD.description: Socially liberal centrist party, the third force in the Commons since 2024. It campaigns on health and care, the environment, electoral reform and rejoining the EU single market.

Con.name: Conservative Party
Con.ideologies: Conservatism, Economic liberalism, British unionism, Euroscepticism
Con.priorities: Lower taxes, Reducing immigration, Fiscal discipline, Defence and support for Ukraine, Leaving the ECHR, full sovereignty
Con.description: The party that governed from 2010 to 2024 and delivered Brexit. In opposition under Kemi Badenoch it favours lower taxes, a smaller state and much lower immigration.

Reform.name: Reform UK
Reform.priorities: Reducing immigration, Leaving the ECHR, full sovereignty, Lower taxes, Cost of living, Security and law and order
Reform.description: Right-wing populist party led by Nigel Farage, which has surged in the polls since 2024. It wants to stop net migration, leave the European Convention on Human Rights, cut taxes and scrap net-zero targets.
